Very disappointing and disturbing experience at Arihant Multispecialist Hospital

We had a deeply painful and traumatic experience at Arihant Multispecialist Hospital. My nani had already passed away by the afternoon, but the hospital staff unnecessarily prolonged the situation till late night, finally declaring it around 3 AM. This felt extremely inhuman and unethical.

What was even more disturbing is that we witnessed the same thing happening to another patient in front of us. It appeared as though patients were being kept on support despite no real hope, only to delay the inevitable.

If the doctors already knew that my nani would not survive, why were we asked to bring her nighty in the afternoon? Why give false hope and drag the family through hours of emotional torture? This raises serious questions about transparency, ethics, and intentions.

At a time when families are already grieving, such behavior adds unnecessary pain and confusion. Hospitals should prioritize honesty, dignity, and compassion — sadly, we experienced none of these here.

I would strongly urge people to think carefully before choosing this hospital for their loved ones.

featured_reviews.name: Durga
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review as an admitted patient who expected transparency, communication, and basic patient care, but unfortunately my experience raised several concerns.

One of my concerns involved the handling of medical supplies during my admission. I noticed items being taken away from my room and, when questioned, I was informed that these were being collected as replacements for items provided by the hospital. However, this process was never explained to me in advance. As a patient, I believe there should be complete transparency regarding any consumables, IV fluids, or medical supplies being used and accounted for, especially when these may ultimately be reflected in the final bill. I had to proactively raise this concern with the hospital administration myself.

My primary concern, however, was regarding the gastroenterology consultation. Throughout the day, I was repeatedly informed by the nursing staff that the gastroenterologist would be visiting me. Whenever I followed up, I was told that the doctor would come but that no one knew when. Even at around 9:30 PM, I was still waiting for clarity regarding the visit.

When I approached the reception desk for an update, I was informed that the gastroenterologist does not usually visit on Saturdays. This directly contradicted the information I had been receiving throughout the day. When I questioned why conflicting information had been provided, the RMO, Dr. Drishti, intervened in the conversation.

Unfortunately, my interaction with Dr. Drishti was disappointing. I found her communication to be dismissive and lacking empathy towards an admitted patient who was unwell and seeking clarity regarding their treatment. Rather than addressing my concern regarding the contradictory information provided by the staff, I was simply told that the doctor would come and that his timing was not fixed. No clear explanation was provided regarding the consultation process, expected timeline, or next steps. Additionally, at no point did the RMO assess my condition, enquire about my health status, or provide reassurance despite my repeated concerns.

As a patient admitted under medical care, I expected better communication, coordination, and accountability. Patients should not be left waiting for hours without updates, nor should they receive conflicting information from different departments regarding specialist consultations.

I would like to acknowledge that several nurses and staff members were caring and professional, and the facilities themselves were good. However, transparency, communication, accountability, and patient engagement require significant improvement. Patients who are admitted, unwell, and paying for specialist care deserve timely information, clear communication, and respectful treatment.

I was admitted to Sapna Hospital for malaria and stayed for 4 days.
It was extremely concerning to see mosquito issues inside the ward while being treated for a mosquito-borne illness. A repellent machine was only provided after repeated complaints.
Hygiene standards were disappointing. I noticed what appeared to be blood stains in saline lines, a dustbin near my bed containing vomit that was not cleared promptly, and an ice pad provided to me that had visible hair on it. Used gloves were also left openly near patient beds instead of being disposed of immediately and bed bugs.
These are basic infection-control practices that should be strictly maintained in any hospital.
Staff behavior at times felt indifferent, and response seemed noticeably quicker when services involved billing.
For a bill of approximately ₹30,000 in just 3 days, I expected a much higher standard of cleanliness, monitoring, and patient care.
I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves hygiene control and patient handling to ensure patient safety.

Today I came to Mumbai and it reminded me of this hospital. In 2024 I admitted my sister here but forgot to write the review. So here it is.

We requested doctor to provide some medicine for getting relief from pain so that we can go back to Gwalior and we will take further treatment there as it is our hometown. But he insisted for getting admitted. Considering the pain we decided for getting admitted. They kept giving my sister injections and medicines for holding the pain. Also ran some other tests. After 24 hours they started insisting for surgery. We finally decided to get discharged from the hospital. The total expense that we had to pay for this 1 day was 30000/-
Worse part was that immediately after the discharge the pain returned and my sister was still in the same situation as 1 day before.
At last I went to a medical store nearby and told him about the pain. The medical store guy gave just 1 pill and with that medicine the entire pain vanished and my sister reached back Gwalior via train without any pain.
In Gwalior she took homeopathy medicine treatment and in six months all the stones are gone without any surgery.

So I'm not sure about how this hospital is at present but in October 2024 they literally looted us in just a single day. So beware.

I am extremely grateful to Dr. Aniket Mishra, his ICU team, and the staff of Aarogyada Hospital for their professionalism, empathy, and exceptional medical care. I strongly recommend this hospital and Dr. Aniket Mishra to anyone seeking reliable and compassionate treatment.
